item.title: Plasma eMTBR-tau as a Biomarker for Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy Tau Tangle Neuropathology
item.description:
Importance: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) is a neurodegenerative disease that cannot accurately be diagnosed during life due to the absence of in vivo biomarkers for CTE neuropathology.

Objective: To evaluate plasma endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region tau (eMTBR-tau) as a candidate biomarker for CTE tau tangle neuropathology.

Design, setting, and participants: This case series included 21 former American-style football players who completed a blood draw as part of participation in clinical research at Boston University beginning April 17, 2008, and who subsequently died, donated their brain, and had completed autopsy by October 9, 2026.

Exposures: Plasma eMTBR-tau nucleic acid-linked immunosandwich assay single-plex immunoassay and plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) (SP-X n = 20; Elecsys n = 1).

Main outcomes and measures: CTE status and stage. Cumulative neuropathologic tau burden scores ranged from 0 to 33 (higher scores indicate tau burden; 0, no tau burden).

Results: Among 21 male brain donors (median age at blood draw, CTE positive: 68 years [IQR, 61-77]; CTE negative: 49 years [IQR, 47-56]), 18 had a neuropathologic diagnosis of CTE. Of these participants, 16 had a diagnosis of high-stage CTE (stage IV = 8, stage III = 8); and 2, of low-stage CTE (stage II = 1, stage I = 1). Five CTE-positive participants had intermediate or high Alzheimer disease neuropathologic change (ADNC). Plasma eMTBR-tau concentration was significantly higher in CTE-positive participants (median, 0.019 pg/mL [IQR, 0.004-0.030]) compared with CTE-negative participants (0.001 pg/mL [IQR, 0.001-0.001]; β = 1.61 [95% CI, 0.51-2.70]). Plasma eMTBR-tau concentrations were highest among CTE-positive participants with comorbid ADNC (0.082 pg/mL [IQR, 0.059-0.131]) and intermediate among those with high-stage CTE without ADNC (n = 11; median, 0.009 pg/mL [IQR, 0.004-0.021]). Plasma eMTBR-tau concentration was significantly higher in high-stage CTE (median, 0.021 pg/mL [IQR, 0.006-0.038]) compared with low-stage CTE (median, 0.001 pg/mL [IQR, 0.001-0.002]; β = 1.79 [95% CI, 0.45-3.13]) or no CTE (median, 0.001 pg/mL [IQR, 0.001-0.001]; β = 1.78 [95% CI, 0.85-2.71]). Differences remained significant after exclusion of 5 cases with comorbid ADNC. Plasma eMTBR-tau concentration was associated with higher cumulative neuropathologic tau burden score across 11 brain regions (β = 0.71 [95% CI, 0.38-1.05]). Plasma p-tau217 concentration was positively associated with eMTBR-tau (β = 0.68 [95% CI, 0.32-1.04]) but was not associated with CTE. P-tau217 concentrations were in the negative range (n = 11) or intermediate range (n = 5) for participants without ADNC copathology. Four participants with ADNC had p-tau217 concentrations in the positive range; and 1, in the intermediate range.

Conclusions and relevance: Participants with high-stage CTE had higher concentrations of plasma eMTBR-tau than those with low-stage or no CTE; concentrations were highest among those with CTE and comorbid ADNC. Plasma eMTBR-tau may represent a feasible biomarker candidate for high-stage CTE tau tangle neuropathology. Larger autopsy and clinical validation studies are needed to establish overall diagnostic accuracy and specificity of plasma eMTBR-tau for CTE neuropathology, in addition to the associated prognostic and clinical implications.

item.title: Medical Imaging and Pediatric and Adolescent Brain Tumor Risk
item.description:
Importance: Ionizing radiation from medical imaging may increase brain tumor risk.

Objective: To quantify brain tumor risk associated with radiation exposure from medical imaging in children and adolescents.

Design, setting, and participants: Retrospective cohort study of children born from 1996 through 2016 who were enrolled from birth in 6 US health care systems or Ontario, Canada, and were alive and cancer-free at age 2 years, with follow-up through December 31, 2017 (US sites), and December 31, 2024 (Ontario).

Exposures: Cumulative radiation dose to the brain from medical imaging, lagged by 2 years.

Main outcomes and measures: Incident brain or other central nervous system tumors. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models for categorical dose, and excess relative risks (ERRs) were estimated using linear dose-response models for continuous dose.

Results: Among 3 704 860 children (1 900 285 [51.3%] male) followed up for 45 671 641 person-years (mean follow-up, 12.3 years), 1536 brain tumors were diagnosed. Mean radiation dose from 1 head computed tomography (CT) examination was 66.2 mGy (SD, 22.2). Among children with cumulative dose of 1 mGy or greater, mean cumulative dose was 73 mGy (SD, 95) overall and 100 mGy (SD, 105) among those diagnosed with brain tumors. Compared with no exposure, brain tumor risk increased with cumulative dose (>0 to <1 mGy: HR, 1.12 [95% CI, 1.01-1.26]; 1 to <5 mGy: HR, 1.71 [95% CI, 0.88-2.96]; 5 to <50 mGy: HR, 1.86 [95% CI, 1.16-2.81]; 50 to <75 mGy: HR, 2.30 [95% CI, 1.64-3.12]; 75 to <100 mGy: HR, 2.02 [95% CI, 1.13-3.30]; 100 to <150 mGy: HR, 2.81 [95% CI, 1.53-4.66]; ≥150 mGy: HR, 3.85 [95% CI, 2.43-5.75]). Cumulative dose was associated with brain tumor risk overall (ERR per 100 mGy, 1.27 [95% CI, 0.83-1.77]; P < .001), with stronger associations for aggressive histologies (ERR per 100 mGy, 1.51 [95% CI, 1.00-2.11]; P < .001). By age 21 years, exposure comparable to 1 head CT was associated with 7.9 excess brain tumors per 10 000 children, or approximately 1 excess tumor per 1266 head CT examinations. The estimated population-attributable fraction was 10.1% (95% CI, 5.8%-14.2%).

Conclusions and relevance: Medical imaging in children and adolescents was associated with a dose-related increase in brain tumor risk. These findings support careful clinical justification and dose minimization when pediatric imaging using ionizing radiation is indicated.

item.title: Toward a Healthier Future Through Obesity Prevention and Care: The JAMA Summit Report on Obesity
item.description:
Importance: Obesity is one of the most difficult challenges of the modern era, affecting more than 1 billion people worldwide. Nearly half of US adults and 1 in 5 US children meet the medical definition of having obesity, with major consequences for cardiometabolic, kidney, hepatic, pulmonary, musculoskeletal, reproductive, oncologic, and mental health. Obesity also carries social and economic harms through stigma, discrimination, and bias.

Observations: Drivers of the obesity epidemic include changes in food production and consumption accompanied by social, economic, and technological shifts that reduce food preparation, disrupt sleep, and decrease physical activity. The burden of these changes is not equally distributed, with higher obesity prevalence among socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. Current prevention measures include nutrition standards, food and menu labeling, school meal policies, sugar-sweetened beverage taxes, community-based lifestyle programs, and public assistance efforts. The impact of these approaches has been inadequate. Contemporary clinical management recognizes obesity as a chronic disease characterized by genetic, biological, and behavioral susceptibilities. Access, affordability, tolerability, and the chronicity of use remain major challenges for all available obesity management strategies, including new glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapies. Potential solutions require a coordinated, multisector response and include efforts to prevent obesity at the societal level, improve care of individuals with obesity, and strengthen research and innovation. Priority areas include improving the food and physical activity environment; strengthening communication and education; strengthening childhood obesity prevention; addressing health inequities; reducing stigma and bias; modernizing obesity care delivery; expanding access to lifestyle, healthy food, medication, and surgical interventions; and supporting long-term treatment adherence and maintenance. Proposed actions include new government policies on food production, labeling, marketing, and school nutrition; modernization of drug evaluation; payment reform to support comprehensive obesity treatment; development of multidisciplinary care models; incentives to promote cross-sector partnerships; and research to advance personalized prevention and treatment strategies.

Conclusions and relevance: The emergence of effective obesity management medications offers a significant opportunity to curb the prevalence of obesity. However, no single intervention will be enough. Sustained improvement will require addressing the underlying structural and environmental drivers of obesity, along with person-centered, multilevel strategies that simultaneously improve prevention, reduce stigma, and expand equitable access to evidence-based treatment. Coordinated action across government, health care systems, clinicians, payers, industry, schools, communities, and researchers will be essential to achieving long-term improvement.

item.title: A Plasma eMTBR-Tau Immunoassay for Detection of Advanced Insoluble Tau Pathology
item.description:
Importance: Blood biomarkers that reflect neurofibrillary tau burden, a defining hallmark of Alzheimer disease (AD), remain limited. Endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region tau 243 (eMTBR-tau243) has shown promise when measured by mass spectrometry; a scalable immunoassay could broaden research access and support clinical evaluation.

Objective: To determine whether plasma levels of eMTBR-tau measured by a novel immunoassay are associated with tau neurofibrillary tangle pathology defined by neuropathology and tau positron emission tomography (PET).

Design, setting, and participants: This cross-sectional study included brain donors with antemortem plasma from 2 US autopsy cohorts, and individuals with plasma samples and tau PET from 2 imaging cohorts in Canada and Sweden, with visits between 2002 and 2025 depending on the cohort.

Exposures: Plasma eMTBR-tau measured with an immunoassay and eMTBR-tau243 measured with mass spectrometry.

Main outcomes and measures: Plasma eMTBR-tau levels across neuropathologic Braak neurofibrillary tangle stages (I-VI, ranging from tangles confined to the entorhinal region to widespread neocortical tangles) and tau-PET Braak stages (0-VI), expressed as fold changes. Correlations with regional tau-PET standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs; higher values indicating more tau tangles), discrimination of regional tau-PET positivity (area under the curve [AUC]), and correlation with mass spectrometry-based eMTBR-tau243.

Results: The study included 728 participants in 4 cohorts (median age by cohort, 71.0-83.5 years; 41.3%-56.6% female). In the 2 autopsy cohorts (n = 241 and n = 240), eMTBR-tau age- and sex-adjusted geometric means were 0.0021 pg/mL and 0.0040 pg/mL, respectively, at Braak stages I-II vs 0.107 pg/mL and 0.101 pg/mL at Braak stage VI (50.5-fold [95% CI, 26.3-97.0] and 25.2-fold [95% CI, 15.8-40.3] higher for stage VI vs stages I-II; P < .001 for both cohorts). In one imaging cohort (n = 99), compared with tau-PET Braak stage 0, eMTBR-tau levels were 11.0-fold (95% CI, 6.9-17.5) higher at stages III-IV and 59.9-fold (95% CI, 39.5-90.7) higher at stages V-VI. Among participants positive for amyloid-β (Aβ) in another imaging cohort (n = 50), the Spearman rank correlations for eMTBR-tau with tau-PET SUVRs were ρ = 0.52 (95% CI, 0.28-0.70) in Braak regions I-II, 0.76 (95% CI, 0.61-0.86) in regions III-IV, and 0.85 (95% CI, 0.75-0.91) in regions V-VI (all P < .001). Immunoassay and mass spectrometry measurements were strongly correlated (Spearman rank correlation, ρ = 0.93 in all participants [n = 108] and ρ = 0.96 in Aβ-positive participants [n = 54]) and discriminated tau-PET positivity similarly (n = 102; AUC range, 0.96-0.99 for the immunoassay and 0.97-0.99 for mass spectrometry).

Conclusions and relevance: A plasma eMTBR-tau immunoassay identified neocortical tau pathology in autopsy and tau-PET cohorts and correlated strongly with mass spectrometry measurements, a proof of principle that eMTBR-tau can be measured by immunoassay as a marker of advanced neurofibrillary tangle pathology.

item.title: Once-Weekly Ribupatide for Weight Loss in Adults in China With Overweight or Obesity: The GEMINI-1 Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: Obesity is a major health problem in China; more pharmacotherapy choices for long-term weight management are needed.

Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, for weight loss in adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes.

Design, setting, and participants: This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 clinical trial was conducted at 55 sites in China. From May to June 2024, adults without diabetes who had a body mass index of 28 or greater or 24 or greater with at least 1 weight-related comorbidity were enrolled, with final follow-up on June 20, 2025.

Interventions: Participants were randomized to receive once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide (target doses of 2 mg, 4 mg, or 6 mg) or matching placebo for 48 weeks, with dose escalation for up to 20 weeks and concomitant lifestyle intervention.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was change in body weight from baseline to week 48, including percent change in body weight and the percentage of participants achieving at least 5% body weight reduction, analyzed under the treatment policy estimand.

Results: Among 567 randomized participants (309 [54.5%] female; mean [SD] age was 34.4 [8.4] years, body weight was 93.0 [17.3] kg, and body mass index was 33.3 [4.5]), 514 (90.7%) completed the 48-week treatment period. Least-squares mean percentage changes in body weight at week 48 were -10.7%, -16.4%, and -17.7% with ribupatide 2, 4, and 6 mg, respectively, vs -1.4% with placebo. At week 48, the placebo-adjusted differences in percentage change in body weight were -9.3 (95% CI, -11.4 to -7.3) percentage points with ribupatide 2 mg, -15.0 (95% CI, -17.1 to -12.9) percentage points with ribupatide 4 mg, and -16.3 (95% CI, -18.4 to -14.2) percentage points with ribupatide 6 mg (P < .001 for all). For at least 5% body weight reduction at week 48, the multiply imputed response rates were 68.1% (95% CI, 59.9% to 75.3%) for ribupatide 2 mg (97 of 142), 88.0% (95% CI, 81.3% to 92.6%) for ribupatide 4 mg (124 of 141), 85.7% (95% CI, 78.6% to 90.7%) with ribupatide 6 mg (121 of 141), and 16.0% (95% CI, 10.8% to 23.1%) with placebo (23 of 143). Placebo-adjusted differences for ribupatide 2, 4, and 6 mg were 52.0 (95% CI, 42.2 to 61.9), 72.0 (95% CI, 63.7 to 80.2), and 69.7 (95% CI, 61.1 to 78.3) percentage points, respectively (all P < .001). The most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events with ribupatide were gastrointestinal events, occurring in 47.9%, 58.2%, and 63.1% of participants receiving ribupatide 2 mg, 4 mg, and 6 mg, respectively, compared with 23.1% receiving placebo; most were mild to moderate in severity and few participants (0.7%) permanently discontinued study treatment because of adverse events.

Conclusions and relevance: Among adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes, once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide resulted in significantly greater weight loss at 48 weeks. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent tolerability findings.

Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06396429.

item.title: Tirzepatide in Adolescents With Obesity: The SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: Information on the effects of tirzepatide, a once-weekly glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist approved for obesity management in adults with obesity, remains limited in adolescents.

Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly tirzepatide in adolescents with obesity or overweight with at least 1 obesity-related complication.

Design, setting, and participants: This phase 3, randomized, double-blind, 72-week clinical trial was conducted at 31 medical research centers and hospitals in Canada, the Czech Republic, Israel, Italy, Poland, and the US from October 16, 2023, to June 2, 2026, among adolescents aged 12 years to younger than 18 years with obesity or overweight with at least 1 obesity-related complication.

Interventions: Participants were randomized 2:1 to receive once-weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide, escalated to a maximum tolerated dose (5, 10, or 15 mg), or placebo for 72 weeks, in addition to healthy lifestyle intervention.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary end point was percent change in body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) from baseline to week 72. Key secondary end points included percentages of participants achieving BMI reductions of at least 5%, at least 10%, at least 15%, and at least 20%; changes in BMI SD score; BMI expressed as a percentage of the 95th percentile; and body weight, waist circumference, and physical functioning from baseline to week 72. Safety outcomes included treatment-emergent adverse events, serious adverse events, and discontinuations due to adverse events.

Results: A total of 160 participants were randomized to receive tirzepatide (n = 109) or placebo (n = 51). Mean (SD) age at baseline was 14.6 (1.6) years, 99 participants (61.9%) were female, mean body weight was 109.7 kg, and mean BMI was 38.6. At week 72, tirzepatide was associated with 18.5% reduction in BMI, compared with 0.5% increase in BMI with placebo, demonstrating superiority over placebo (estimated treatment difference, -19.0 [95% CI, -23.9 to -14.1] percentage points; P < .001). Of 10 key secondary outcomes, all demonstrated statistically significant differences favoring tirzepatide compared with placebo. Overall, 79.6% of tirzepatide-treated participants achieved BMI reduction of at least 5% compared with 28.5% of participants in the placebo group (risk difference, 51.2 [95% CI, 36.3-66.1] percentage points; P < .001). The most common adverse events with tirzepatide treatment were gastrointestinal (mostly mild to moderate).

Conclusions and relevance: In adolescents with obesity or overweight with obesity-related complications, tirzepatide, in addition to healthy lifestyle intervention, led to significant reductions in percent change in BMI compared with placebo at 72 weeks.

Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06075667.

item.title: Fluid eMTBR-tau243 as a Biomarker of Mixed 3-Repeat and 4-Repeat Tau Pathology
item.description:
Importance: Neurodegenerative diseases with abnormal tau protein aggregation in the brain (ie, tauopathies) can be classified by the tau isoform that accumulates: 3-repeat (3R), 4-repeat (4R), or mixed 3R/4R tauopathies, which include chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), some forms of frontotemporal lobar degeneration, and Alzheimer disease (AD). The endogenously cleaved form of tau microtubule binding region containing the residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) can be detected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and blood and has been associated with AD tau pathology, but its specificity and biological interpretation in non-AD tauopathies remains unclear.

Objective: To evaluate biofluid eMTBR-tau243 in a range of tauopathies.

Design, setting, and participants: This case-control study included 4 biorepositories based in the US that contributed CSF and plasma samples from participants with and without tauopathies, many of whom had antemortem biofluid samples paired with autopsy or genetically defined neuropathology. Samples were analyzed between August 2023 and December 2025. Data analysis occurred from August 2024 to July 2026.

Exposure: CSF and plasma eMTBR-tau243 concentrations measured using a mass spectrometry-based assay.

Main outcomes and measures: Outcomes included mixed 3R/4R tauopathy (eg, AD and CTE) based on autopsy, frontotemporal lobar degeneration with MAPT variants (FTLD-MAPT), and CTE stage. Differences in biomarker levels between groups were evaluated using analysis of variance or analysis of covariance, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was calculated to evaluate the discriminative performance of fluid eMTBR-tau243.

Results: Among the 229 participants (196 with CSF samples and 55 with plasma samples [22 with both]), mean (SD) age at fluid sample collection was 63 (13) years and 108 (47%) were female. Median (IQR) CSF eMTBR-tau243 was increased in 10 patients with AD (0.459 [0.246-0.801] fmol/mL) compared with 29 cognitively unimpaired controls (0.002 [0.001-0.005] fmol/mL) (adjusted P < .001), but other autopsy-confirmed non-AD tauopathies (which included 52 individuals with conditions including progressive supranuclear palsy and corticobasal degeneration) did not demonstrate an increase (0.015 [0.008, 0.039] fmol/mL). Six symptomatic FTLD-MAPT variant carriers with mixed 3R/4R tauopathy (R406W, V337M, and G389R) had increased median (IQR) CSF eMTBR-tau243 (0.140 [0.055-0.174] fmol/mL) compared with 15 4R tauopathy variant carriers including N279K and P301L (0.004 [0.001-0.044] fmol/mL) (P = .001). Median (IQR) plasma eMTBR-tau243 was increased in 11 patients with CTE (1.93 [0.42-3.68] fmol/L) compared with 20 cognitively unimpaired controls (0.29 [0.05-0.62] fmol/L) (adjusted P = .007), but did not increase as high as among 14 patients with AD (11.25 [2.29-19.38] fmol/L). Plasma eMTBR-tau243 distinguished CTE stage III and IV from controls (AUC, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.92-1.00), but not CTE stage I from controls (AUC, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.32-0.97).

Conclusions and relevance: This study found that plasma and CSF eMTBR-tau243 were increased in mixed 3R/4R tauopathies including AD, high-stage CTE, and a subset of genetic FTLD-MAPT, compared with cognitively unimpaired controls. Further validation in larger cohorts is needed to determine the clinical utility of eMTBR-tau243 as a potential diagnostic biomarker for CTE and other tauopathies beyond AD.

Horie K, Koppisetti RK, VandeVrede L, Asken BM, Li Y, Yen D
